items.title: Xaluritamig Phase 1 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing the safety of xaluritamig, a new drug, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The study is currently recruiting patients to determine safe dosing levels. This is a Phase 1 trial, which means it's an early investigation focused on safety rather than effectiveness.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This large Phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig plus abiraterone against standard treatments (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy yet. The study measures overall survival and is currently recruiting. This is a major trial that could change treatment options if successful.

items.title: Stereotactic Radiotherapy for Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer (HIMARS)
items.summary: This trial tests precisely targeted radiation therapy on bone and lymph node metastases in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer that no longer responds to chemotherapy. The study aims to identify how much tumor volume can be safely treated and whether this approach reduces pain and complications. Focuses on quality of life improvements for advanced disease.

items.title: VIR-5500 Phase 1 Trial in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial evaluates VIR-5500 (AMX-500) alone and in combination with androgen receptor inhibitors in prostate cancer patients. The study includes dose escalation and expansion phases to determine safety and preliminary effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients for this first-in-human study.

items.title: INV-9956 Phase 1/2 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial evaluates the safety and effectiveness of INV-9956, a new drug, in patients with advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study combines Phase 1 (safety testing) and Phase 2 (effectiveness evaluation) and is currently recruiting patients. This represents a novel treatment approach for advanced disease.

items.title: Sacituzumab Govitecan Phase 2 Trial After AR-Directed Therapy Failure
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies sacituzumab govitecan (an antibody-drug conjugate) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose disease progressed after treatment with drugs like enzalutamide or abiraterone. The trial is no longer recruiting new patients but continues following enrolled participants. Explores treatment options after standard therapies fail.

items.title: Proton Therapy vs IMRT for Recurrent Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial compares two types of radiation therapy (proton beam and IMRT) for prostate cancer that has returned or spread to a limited number of sites after initial treatment. The study uses shorter treatment courses and is evaluating side effects and effectiveness. No longer recruiting but following enrolled patients.

items.title: Duration Trial: Radiation Plus Hormone Therapy With/Without Abiraterone
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial investigates whether adding abiraterone to standard radiation and hormone therapy improves quality of life in patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer (spread to limited sites). The study compares 8-9 months of combination therapy against standard treatment alone. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Inavolisib Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests inavolisib plus enzalutamide compared to alternative treatments in biomarker-selected patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have already received one prior AR-targeted therapy. The study uses specific genetic markers to identify patients most likely to benefit. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Abiraterone With/Without Cabazitaxel After Docetaxel in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies whether adding chemotherapy (cabazitaxel) to hormone therapy (abiraterone plus antiandrogen) works better than hormone therapy alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with docetaxel. The study is no longer recruiting but continues following enrolled patients.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Plus Luxdegalutamide Phase 1/2 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial evaluates the combination of tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) and luxdegalutamide (a novel AR inhibitor) versus standard care in progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study includes dose-finding and effectiveness evaluation phases. Currently recruiting patients for this novel combination approach.

items.title: AMO959 Plus Lutetium-PSMA Plus ARPI Phase 1b/2 Trial
items.summary: This Phase 1b/2 trial combines AMO959 with lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy and an AR inhibitor in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness of this triple combination in chemotherapy-naive patients who failed one prior AR-targeted therapy. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Zanzalintinib After Pluvicto Phase 2 Trial in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial will study zanzalintinib (a drug targeting cancer growth pathways) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have already received Pluvicto (lutetium-PSMA therapy) but haven't had chemotherapy. The study aims to determine if this approach is effective after radioligand therapy. Not yet recruiting.

items.title: TERPS Trial for Newly Diagnosed Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies treatment approaches for prostate cancer patients who present with a limited number of metastases at initial diagnosis (de novo oligometastatic disease). The study aims to improve outcomes in this specific patient population. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Opevesostat Phase 3 Trial vs Alternative Hormone Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: This large Phase 3 trial compares opevesostat (MK-5684) plus hormone replacement therapy against switching to alternative hormone agents (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who previously received one AR-targeted therapy. The study measures progression-free survival and includes patients with and without AR mutations. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Creatine and Resistance Training Phase 3 Trial for Muscle Preservation
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether creatine supplementation combined with twice-weekly telehealth resistance training can preserve muscle mass and reduce cancer progression in prostate cancer patients. The 52-week program aims to reduce fatigue, improve physical function, and enhance quality of life. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Combinations Phase 1/2 Trial for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial evaluates tulmimetostat combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (earlier stage than castration-resistant). The study assesses safety and effectiveness of these combinations in patients with newly metastatic or recurrent disease. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Multiple Radioligand Therapy Phase 1 Trial for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial uses specialized imaging to identify which target (PSMA, SSTR2, or GRPR) is most expressed on tumor cells, then treats with the corresponding radioligand therapy in patients with metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer. The study evaluates how treatment changes target expression over time. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Enzalutamide With/Without Radium-223 Phase 2 Trial in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial compares enzalutamide (an AR inhibitor) alone versus enzalutamide plus radium-223 (a radioactive treatment for bone metastases) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study tests whether combining these treatments works better than hormone therapy alone. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Terbium-161-PSMA Phase 1 Trial in Taiwan for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This first-in-Taiwan Phase 1 trial evaluates 161Tb-PSMA-I&T, a new generation PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy using Terbium-161 instead of Lutetium-177. The study assesses safety, how the drug distributes in the body, and preliminary effectiveness in Taiwanese men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial as First-Line mCRPC Treatment
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares the combination of olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) plus abiraterone against abiraterone alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who haven't received prior chemotherapy or new hormone agents at the mCRPC stage. The study measures survival and safety. No longer recruiting but following patients.

items.title: SX-682 Plus Enzalutamide Phase 2 Trial After ARPI Failure
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies the combination of SX-682 (an immune modulator) plus enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have failed prior AR-targeted therapy. The trial explores whether this combination can overcome resistance to hormone treatments. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests two doses of luxdegalutamide (a novel AR inhibitor) combined with abiraterone versus standard AR therapy in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study aims to select the best dose for Phase 3 trials. Currently recruiting patients with earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibition Overcomes Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed new dual-target drugs that simultaneously inhibit BRD4 and AKT pathways to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Laboratory studies showed that compound 21d effectively addressed the resistance that develops when AKT inhibitors are used alone. This represents a novel strategy for drug-resistant disease.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Scientists developed and validated a machine learning model that predicts overall survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who don't undergo surgery. The study of over 3,000 patients found that Gleason score (tumor aggressiveness) is the most important factor for prognosis, more so than tumor stage. This tool could help personalize treatment decisions.

items.title: New ALDH7A1 Inhibitors Show Promise for Prostate Cancer Treatment
items.source: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
items.summary: Researchers identified new drugs that selectively target ALDH7A1, a protein that drives prostate cancer growth and contributes to castration-resistant disease. These covalent inhibitors represent the first selective compounds against this target and open new treatment possibilities. This is early laboratory research identifying a potential new drug target.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic CRPC Show Mixed Results
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 trials with 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors show modest benefits overall. One-year survival was 63% and median progression-free survival was short. Combination therapies showed better results than single-drug approaches. The data suggests ICIs may work better when combined with other treatments.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Preserves Bone Health During Enzalutamide Plus ADT Treatment
items.summary: The BonEnza Phase 2 trial found that adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening drug) to enzalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy significantly improved bone mineral density in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients after 18 months. Without zoledronic acid, patients experienced bone density loss. This supports bone protection strategies during intensive hormone therapy.
